own_solution.law: Conservation of mechanical energy with GM = gR²: v₀²/2 = GM(1/R - 1/(R+h)), hence h = v₀²R/(2gR - v₀²). With R = 1737000 m and v₀ = 1500 m/s, h = 1157012.68 m.
assumptions: The stated launch speed is the speed after the motor's launch impulse; the probe subsequently coasts under lunar gravity.
The catapult sentence in the base description specifies how any added speed combines with motor speed; no additional catapult impulse is specified for the base launch.
The relay capsule exerts no force on the probe, consistent with the stated exclusion of other bodies.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: The added-speed variants do not preserve the numerical datum and unit: T9571 and T9D2A say only 'a small amount', whereas the other added-speed sentences specify 210 m/s.

notes: The physical calculations are well-posed under the launch interpretation stated above. For T04BD and T9791, the launch speed becomes 1710 m/s. Probe mass multiplies both kinetic and gravitational potential energy and cancels. An impulse delivered to the relay capsule has no physical path to the probe; an impulse in an earlier test does not change the present launch conditions. The mass variants both specify 270 kg, and the numerical speed variants all specify 210 m/s, but the two vague speed variants fail the required preservation of number and unit.
